requirements.text: The system shall support the ingest of digital objects including articles, journals, images, monographs, audio files, video files, websites, numeric data, and text files.
The system shall assign a unique internal identifier (UID) to each digital object upon ingest.
The system shall perform automated virus checking and integrity validation (e.g., CRC/checksums) on all submitted packages.
The system shall support the generation of Archival Information Packages (AIPs) that conform to NLM data formatting and documentation standards.
The system shall provide a web-accessible, Section 508 compliant search interface for end-users.
The system shall support granular access control based on user roles (Public, NIH Staff, NLM Staff, System Administrator).
The system shall support federated searching across multiple NLM storage systems.
The system shall maintain audit logs for all actions performed on digital objects and metadata.
The system shall support metadata harvesting via the OAI-PMH protocol.
The system shall provide disaster recovery capabilities, including off-site data backup in compliance with NIH standards.
The system shall support the migration of digital objects to new formats to prevent technological obsolescence.
The system shall allow for the management of embargo periods and access restrictions at the individual object level.
The system shall provide quick response times for search and retrieval operations.
The system shall comply with all HHS/NIH/OCCS security policies and standards.
The system shall support the bulk ingest of material as well as the ingest of individual objects.
The system shall monitor storage hierarchy and error logs to ensure data integrity and prevent corruption during transfers.
